seoTitle: How to Add a Page in Confluence Easily (2026 Guide)
metaDescription: Create a new page in Confluence: the Create button and its template panel, the slash command for inserting content, and how drafts stay private until Publish.
intro: A Confluence space is only as useful as the pages inside it, and creating a new one is one of the most common actions you'll take in the app. This guide walks through the entry points for starting a page, what a blank page looks like before you've typed anything, and how the slash command turns an empty page into a structured document with tables, panels, and embedded widgets, without hunting through menus to find each block type.
prerequisites: Add content permission in the space you're creating the page in

steps.heading: Start from the For you screen
steps.body: Confluence's "For you" landing page is built around getting you into something quickly: a row of large cards at the top offers Create a page, Set up a team space, Brainstorm on a whiteboard, and Create a team profile, and below that sits a row of recommended templates like Project plan, Strategic plan, and Simple retrospective. Clicking Create page from here skips navigating into a specific space first; Confluence prompts you for that as part of the creation flow. The same result is reachable from any screen through the Create button in the top right, which also offers Create with Rovo, Confluence's AI-assisted option that starts a page from a short written description instead of a blank canvas.

image.caption: The "For you" home screen, with a Create page card alongside quick-start options for spaces, whiteboards, and team profiles.

steps.heading: Land on a blank page
steps.body: A freshly created page opens with just a placeholder title, "Give this page a title", and a prompt below it reading "Type / to insert elements." A set of quick-start templates is offered alongside the blank canvas (1-on-1 Meeting, 4 Ls Retrospective, 5 Whys Analysis, and a link to "All templates"), worth a glance before typing from scratch, since a lot of common page types already have a structured starting layout built for them.

image.caption: A brand-new blank page, with the title placeholder, the slash-command hint, and quick-access template buttons along the bottom.

steps.heading: Give the page a real title
steps.body: Click into the title field and replace the placeholder with something specific. Vague titles like "Untitled" or "Notes" make a page nearly impossible to find later once a space has more than a handful of pages in it. In this example the page becomes "PMN Online Support", immediately telling anyone browsing the sidebar what they'll find inside without opening it. Confluence autosaves as you work, shown by the "Saved" indicator next to the Publish button in the top right, and the page stays private to you until it's published or explicitly shared, so there's no risk of a half-finished title going public.

image.caption: The page renamed to "PMN Online Support," with the body still empty and ready for the first block of content.

steps.heading: Insert content with the slash command
steps.body: Type / anywhere in the body to open Confluence's element picker, then keep typing to filter it: typing /w, for instance, surfaces Whiteboard, Widget Connector, Watched Issues, Warning panel, Work Item Statistics, and Workload Pie Chart, each with a short description of what it does. Instead of hunting through toolbar icons, you type a few letters of what you want and pick it from the filtered list, whether that's a table, an info panel, or an embedded widget pulling in content from another tool.

image.caption: The slash-command menu filtered to "/w," listing insertable elements like Whiteboard, Widget Connector, and Work Item Statistics.

steps.heading: Nest it under the right parent in the sidebar
steps.body: Where a page sits in the sidebar hierarchy matters as much as its title. A support page buried three levels under an unrelated project folder won't get found by browsing. Drag the page under its intended parent in the Content tree, or create it directly from the "+" next to an existing page so it nests correctly from the start. Confluence shows the full hierarchy in the left sidebar, so you can confirm the placement before moving on.

steps.heading: Publish when it's ready
steps.body: New and edited pages sit in an unpublished, autosaved draft, visible only to you until you click Publish in the top right. This gives you room to build out the structure, add a template, and insert your first few blocks without anyone else seeing a half-finished page. Once it looks right, Publish pushes it live to the space, at which point it becomes visible to everyone with access and searchable across the site. Confluence also offers a Schedule publish option from the same panel, for setting a page to go live at a specific date and time instead of immediately.

faq.question: Where do I start creating a new page in Confluence?
faq.answer: From the "For you" home screen, click the Create a page card, or use the Create button in the top right of any screen, which also offers a Create with Rovo option for starting from an AI-generated draft. Both manual paths lead to the same blank-page editor.

faq.question: Do I need special permission to create a page?
faq.answer: Yes. You need Add content permission for the space you're creating it in. Without that permission, the option to create a page in that space won't be available.

faq.question: How do I insert tables, panels, or widgets into a Confluence page?
faq.answer: Type / anywhere in the page body to open the element picker, then keep typing to filter it: for example, /w surfaces Whiteboard, Widget Connector, and other elements starting with W.

faq.question: Are Confluence pages saved automatically while I'm editing, and can others see a draft?
faq.answer: Yes, they're autosaved as you work. Unpublished drafts stay private to you and aren't visible to teammates until you publish or explicitly share them.

faq.question: Can I start a page from a template instead of a blank page?
faq.answer: Yes. The page editor offers quick-start templates like 1-on-1 Meeting and 5 Whys Analysis alongside the blank option, and the "All templates" link opens the full template library.

faq.question: How do I control where a page sits in my space's page tree?
faq.answer: Drag it under the correct parent page in the sidebar's Content list, or create it directly from the "+" icon next to the page you want it nested under, so the hierarchy is right from the start.

verifiedNote: Click path and screens come from a walkthrough recorded in 2025. The Create button, its Create with Rovo option, the Add content permission requirement, autosave behavior, and draft privacy were re-checked against Atlassian's official Confluence Cloud documentation in September 2026 and are new to this pass. The slash-command mechanics and the "For you" landing screen match what the recording shows but weren't independently confirmed against that same page, since Atlassian's docs describe the template picker as a side panel, not the bottom row of buttons the screenshots show; both may be accurate for different entry points, and neither claim is stated here as more certain than it is.
